The SC offer: 'an offer I could not resist'; became CJ in 2005; 'most importantly, I would not have reached the Court at all, were it not for my association with then Gen. Fidel V. Ramos in the Rotary Club of Manila'

stances.claim: CJP's path to the Supreme Court was Rotary-enabled: Ramos observed him during his Rotary presidency (1990-1991), was impressed by his printed workbook and their conversations about law and good government, and used those observations to form his judgment about CJP's competence and character. Without Rotary, there would have been no Chief Justice Panganiban.
stances.rhetorical_move: Rotary-as-career-enabler: the civic organization as the unseen institutional conduit for judicial appointment -- with implications for all Rotarians about the value of civic engagement

stances.claim: The Air Quality Monitoring project is a qualitative upgrade in RC Makati's mission: from charity work for the poor to 'a call for life worth living on Planet Earth' that serves everyone. The project deserves the club's full financial commitment -- CJP puts his own P50,000 where his endorsement is.
stances.rhetorical_move: lead-gift endorsement: CJP's first P50,000 donation as the performative proof of his endorsement and as a call to action for the 120 members
stances.confidence: asserted and performed (check handed over publicly)

notable_anecdotes: Ramos's candid admission: 'I know you did not campaign for me. You did not even vote for me. You voted for your mentor, Jovy Salonga. But that is alright. What matters is I know you to be competent, honest and honorable.' -- the most direct compliment on CJP's character from a Philippine president.

The printed workbook: Ramos was impressed that along with his inaugural speech as Rotary Club of Manila President, CJP 'had produced and distributed a printed workbook showing my vision, mission, values, projects and work plan to achieve those projects.' -- the governance toolkit that caught a president's eye.

The seatmate moral: 'love your seatmate during Rotary meetings. He may just change your career, as Rotarian Eddie Ramos did to the career of Rotarian Art Panganiban. Who knows, Eddie Yap may turn out to be the Eddie Ramos in the life of every Makati Rotarian!'

Eddie Yap's 6Gs (in the foreword to 'Stirred, Not Shaken'): 'impresario, art connoisseur, sous-chef, civic leader and bon vivant masquerading as a financial wizard, real estate specialist, executive nonpareil, stock market hotshot, budget expert and even a level-headed constitutionalist. The good news is that he is all these pursuits. And the better news is that he is a master of all of them.' -- to which CJP added 2 more Gs (gold and golden president) at the anniversary.

CJP's public P50,000 donation: 'so that my endorsement will not be only lip service to your laudable project, let me have the honor of contributing the first P50,000 today with this check' -- the performative lead gift.

one_paragraph_summary: Delivered July 17, 2015 as the Guest of Honor speech at the Rotary Club of Makati's 50th anniversary, this address by CJP -- initially reluctant to accept as he had 'retired from active public life eight and a half years ago' -- opens with an expanded tribute to President Eddie Yap: in the foreword to his book 'Stirred, Not Shaken' (launched October 13, 2014 on his 70th birthday), CJP described him as an impresario, art connoisseur, sous-chef, civic leader and bon vivant masquerading as a financial wizard and constitutionalist -- 'a master of all of them' (6Gs: gab, giving, genius); today CJP adds 2 more: gold (Golden President for the Golden Year). The speech's centerpiece is CJP's testimony that 'it was Rotary that enabled me to enter the exalted and forbidding door of the Supreme Court': on June 17, 1992, President-elect Ramos invited him to a one-on-one and offered the Secretary of Justice post (declined); Ramos then offered the SC, revealing he had observed CJP 'closely during my Rotary presidency' and was impressed by his printed workbook (vision, mission, values, projects, work plan) and by their seatmate conversations about law and good government -- 'I know you did not campaign for me. You did not even vote for me. You voted for your mentor, Jovy Salonga. But that is alright. What matters is I know you to be competent, honest and honorable.' The moral: 'love your seatmate during Rotary meetings. He may just change your career, as Rotarian Eddie Ramos did to the career of Rotarian Art Panganiban. Who knows, Eddie Yap may turn out to be the Eddie Ramos in the life of every Makati Rotarian!' He then endorses the 50th anniversary project -- an Air Quality Monitoring and Reporting System at five Metro Manila locations (pilot: P600,000; full country: P6 million; 120 members at P50,000 each) -- and hands President Eddie a P50,000 check on the spot: 'so that my endorsement will not be only lip service.'
